criteria: Adriaen's criteria for this review: a finding matters by how much it improves the game for the player (bugs and glitches they can see, how the camp looks on a phone, smoothness and load time on a phone) or how much it speeds up development, including AI-driven iteration (honest checks, accurate comments, no stale numbers, fast and trustworthy bakes). Use as few triangles as still look good: spend them on silhouettes and things seen up close, paint detail into colours or textures, and never let tools add hidden detail (caps nobody sees, subdivision for bakes, high segment counts on small parts); state triangle counts per object for every exported model. Keep every asset variant (the plush, baby and plush_real sloth styles, and the flat sticker set). Anything that changes how something looks or how the game behaves is Adriaen's pick, and removals or retiring options are his decision on scope. Fixes that need a GPU light rebake are batched so one rebake covers them.

findings.title: The removed PCFSoftShadowMap makes the first frame recompile almost every shader, which wastes compileAsync
findings.group: A: fix now, no rebake, no pick
findings.evidence: jeep.js sets renderer.shadowMap.type = THREE.PCFSoftShadowMap. In three 0.186.1, WebGLShadowMap.render (lines 99-102) warns 'PCFSoftShadowMap has been removed. Using PCFShadowMap instead.' and changes the type to PCFShadowMap, but only on the first shadow render, the first frame (campGround.js sets needsUpdate). compileAsync in main.js:75 runs before that, with type 2. WebGLPrograms puts parameters.shadowMapType into every program's cache key (line 489), and setProgram re-runs getProgram on each material's first real draw, so every program compiled during the loading card is thrown away and compiled again synchronously on the first frames. Verifier: Confirmed in three 0.186.1 source (/home/claude/sloth/node_modules/three/src/renderers/webgl/WebGLShadowMap.js:99-102 switches type to PCFShadowMap only inside render(); WebGLPrograms.js:364/489 puts shadowMapType in every program key). jeep.js:57 still sets PCFSoftShadowMap.
findings.fix: Use THREE.PCFShadowMap in jeep.js:57. That is what three already renders with, so the picture is unchanged. Optionally check in camp-probe that the linked-program count does not grow after __ready.

findings.title: His smile never goes away: the happy clip is reset every frame and never stopped
findings.group: A: fix now, no rebake, no pick
findings.evidence: The smile is held with `hp.timeScale = 0`. three's isRunning() returns false when timeScale is 0, so `smile && !hp.isRunning()` is true on every smiling frame (reset, play, time = 1.5), and `!smile && hp.isRunning()` is never true, so hp.stop() never runs. Node sim with three@0.186.1: 100 smiling frames gave 100 resets, and the action was still active at weight 1 after the smile ended. So after his first line he keeps a smile blended in for the rest of the session. It also halves the sleep blink (blink, happy and the base clip are averaged), so his eyes are not fully shut when asleep. opApi.dbg filters on isRunning, so it hides this. Verifier: Confirmed at headPose.js:51. In three, isRunning() is false when timeScale===0, so the smile is reset every smiling frame and hp.stop() never runs. Once he smiles, it stays blended in for good.
findings.fix: Keep a flag such as op.anim.smiling. Start the smile once on the change to true (or use hp.paused = true instead of timeScale 0) and call hp.fadeOut(0.3) on the change to false. Set the sleeping blink once on the change of op.sleeping as well (operator-20).

findings.title: Repeated chore toasts make no sound: audio.js hears chores by diffing the toast's DOM text

findings.title: The glade floor painter runs worn() and an edge pass for all 262,144 pixels, though only 7% are ever worn
findings.group: A: fix now, no rebake, no pick
findings.evidence: buildGlade paints the trodden earth by calling worn(wx, wz) for every pixel of the 512x512 canvas. Each call is a segment projection plus pathEnd()'s 12 Math.hypot and a third hypot. Timed in node with the real layout.js and util.js (/tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/5e5ccd13-efc0-592c-83dc-1d72c08220b1/scratchpad/rev2c/props-runtime/glade.mjs): 164 ms on this cloud CPU, with only 18,941 pixels (7.2%) above 0.01. The edge fade (atan2 and hypot per pixel) adds 30 ms. All of it runs on the main thread during start-up, on every load, for an image that is the same every time. Verifier: Confirmed at glade.js:60-67: worn() runs for every one of the 512x512 pixels, and the edge pass at 77-79 does an atan2 and a hypot per pixel. I did not re-time it. A bounding-box loop gives the same output.
findings.fix: Work out the worn area's bounding box once (the segment from `end` to STAND, padded by 1.15 m, plus the last 12 path points padded by 0.8 m) and loop over just those pixels; the output is identical. For the edge fade, skip pixels where r < rim - 0.9 (alpha is 255 there anyway), or paint it with a radial gradient. Expect roughly 10 times less work.

findings.title: Pack passes into colour channels: fire, stove and lanterns in one pass as R, G, B; SUN and SUN_OPEN in one pass
findings.group: B: fix now, then one rebake
findings.where: props/camp/bake_camp_lightmap.py:252-268 (the lights are white, one group per pass), 339-358 (lit[g] = px[..., :3].mean(-1))
findings.evidence: Every receiver and occluder is baked with a neutral grey stand-in (grey(), 0.5 or 1.0). With a neutral albedo, light transport keeps the three colour channels apart, bounces included. So a red fire, a green stove and blue lanterns in one DIFFUSE call give exactly the three channels the script now gets from three calls and then averages to grey. The world strength is 0 for those three groups, so the sky adds nothing to them. In the same way, a red sun lamp that casts shadows and a green one that doesn't (Light.use_shadow = False), pointing the same way, give SUN and SUN_OPEN in one direct-only call. Verifier: The physics holds: neutral grey or white stand-ins, white lamps (line 254), world strength 0 for fire, stove and lanterns (only(), line 286). Three lamp colours would keep the three channels apart. Risk: Cycles' light tree and many-light sampling weigh lights by power and luminance.
findings.fix: Colour each light group's lamps (1,0,0), (0,1,0), (0,0,1), read channels 0 to 2 instead of the mean, and do the same for the sun pair. Many-light sampling now splits samples among more lamps, so give the RGB pass about 1.5x samples; check its noise against today's maps. Estimated saving: about 2 x 175 s + 130 s = 8 min at today's settings, about 1 to 2 min once the 2048 and per-pass-sample changes are in (estimate). The light is physically the same, so no new look to pick, but A/B it once.
